'''Roland Glowinski''' (9 March 1937 – 26 January 2022) was a French-American mathematician. He obtained his PhD in 1970 from [[Jacques-Louis Lions]]<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=12407}}</ref> and was known for his work in [[applied mathematics]], in particular numerical solution and applications of [[partial differential equations]] and [[variational inequality|variational inequalities]]. He was a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and held an [[endowed chair]] at the [[University of Houston]] from 1985. Glowinski wrote many books on the subject of mathematics. In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>

==Selected publications==
*with [[Jacques-Louis Lions]] and Raymond Trémolières: Numerical Analysis of variational inequalities, North Holland 1981<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1983-15096-6|title=Book Review: ''Numerical analysis of variational inequalities''|year=1983|last1=Hager|first1=William W.|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=8|pages=100–103|doi-access=free}}</ref> [https://books.google.com/books?id=Pf4ed2mtbx4C 2011 pbk edition]
*Numerical methods for nonlinear variational problems, Springer Verlag 1984, 2008; [https://books.google.com/books?id=vGrwCAAAQBAJ 2013 pbk edition]
*with Michel Fortin: Augmented Lagrangian methods : applications to the numerical solution of boundary-value problems, North Holland 1983
*with Patrick Le Tallec: [https://books.google.com/books?id=gx_iibBqEl8C Augmented Lagrangian and operator-splitting methods in nonlinear mechanics], Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics 1989

Finite element methods for incompressible viscous flows|series=Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. IX|isbn = 9780444512246|last1 = Glowinski|first1 = R.|year = 2003 |publisher=North-Holland}}<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-05-01818-1|title=Book Review: ''Numerical analysis for fluids, Part 3.
